algorithm.title: Identification and Treatment of Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome.

cell.label: Identify newborns who may have been exposed in utero to opioids or other drugs of abuse: maternal history, urine drug screen, infant drug screen, or suspicion of undisclosed drug use (lack of prenatal care, maternal stigmata of drug use, sexually transmitted disease).
Minimize stimuli, employ small calorically dense feedings, swaddle gently. Monitor for signs of neonatal abstinence using a standardized symptom instrument (). Scores require pharmacologic treatment?
Initiate morphine-containing regimen at 0.4 mg/kg/day in 6 divided doses. Titrate up 20%/day until symptoms controlled. Seizures?
Symptoms controlled and good weight gain before reaching maximum dose (~1.25 mg/kg/day morphine).
Wean 10%/day as guided by symptom scores. Infant with controlled symptoms?
When morphine is discontinued, monitor for at least 2 days in an inpatient setting prior to discharge from hospital.
Resume last dose at which symptoms controlled; wean as tolerated.
Phenobarbital load with daily dosing. Investigate possible non-withdrawal etiologies.
Monitor for 2-4 days as an inpatient prior to discharge.
